articles.titleTr: Shops looted as German cost-of-living protests turn violent
articles.summaryTr: The protests in cities across Germany - including Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt - came on the same day hundreds of thousands also protested in France.
articles.articleText: Shops looted as German cost-of-living protests turn violent - Published Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday as clashes erupted in German cities over the cost of living. Besides Frankfurt - Germany's financial hub - there were incidents of violence in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg, with police saying they used water cannon to disperse protesters who were targeting emergency workers with fireworks, stones and bottles. Thousands joined largely peaceful demonstrations earlier in the day. They were organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt - meaning "Gen Z takes charge" - to protest against underfunding in schools, the high cost of living, public spending cuts and military service. The unrest in Germany follows similar youth-led mass protests in France, where more than 320,000 people also demonstrated on Saturday. On Sunday, Germany's Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt told Bild newspaper that overnight police had prevented "violence like that seen in Paris" in recent weeks and called for "harsh punishments" for rioters and looters. Overnight, a large section of Frankfurt's main shopping street was closed off by police. A police spokesperson said many arrests were made in the city. Authorities in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin reported as many as 18,000 protesters, roughly half of what the organisers had estimated on their website. German media say tens of thousands protested in German cities on Saturday. Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina Friedrich said the demonstrations were "to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion". She said: "What matters most to us is better support for the health and education systems. We are against compulsory military service and we are in favour of a fairer distribution of the burden." - Europe's youth is on the march - but does anything actually unite them? - Published3 days ago On Saturday night Frankfurt police said "violent riots" were occurring in the city centre and that special police units had been deployed. The windows of several shops had been smashed and molotov cocktails were thrown at emergency services, police said. Officials said the windows of a gun shop were smashed and that they had seized two weapons after arresting a suspect. People also broke into other shops, stealing items like trainers. Roman Poseck, interior minister of Hesse state, of which Frankfurt is the biggest city, said that "around 100 clearly identified left-wing extremists" had infiltrated the protest in the city. He added that it was "shameful" how the protests had ended. "We all have those images from France in our minds - looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers... France must not be held up as a model in this regard." Police said the situation calmed down overnight into Sunday in the city. Similar instances took place in other German cities, following largely peaceful demonstrations. In Cologne, police said officers were attacked near the main train station, with bottles thrown and a bicycle launched. Cologne's police chief Johannes Hermanns said it was "deeply saddening that young people who wanted to peacefully demonstrate for their future were infiltrated today by extremists who had nothing but violence in mind". A smaller demonstration in the evening in Berlin - following larger protests in the day - resulted in 27 police officers being injured, and up to 56 people temporarily detained, Berlin police said. In Hamburg, people dressed in black set off fireworks and set barricades on fire, with public broadcaster NDR reporting that 120 people were arrested. The protests in Germany took place on the same day as other large-scale demonstrations in Europe. In France, more than 320,000 people took part in a third consecutive weekend of largely peaceful protests in cities across the country, demanding action on the high cost of living and poor public services, especially in the education sector. Thousands of police officers were deployed across the country, and officers fired tear gas at demonstrators in some cities. There were more than 770 arrests across France during the demonstrations on Saturday, roughly half as many as the previous week's protests, the French interior ministry said. French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said a police officer had been injured by a molotov cocktail and French prosecutors later launched an attempted murder probe. Police in Paris said several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles. French protest organisers, the Gilet Jaune, or Yellow Vests, have said dozens of protesters have been seriously injured during recent demonstrations across the country, with many hurt by "grenades". France suspended the use of one type of stun grenade while policing student protests in early October after a 15-year-old's hand was blown off, but French newspaper Le Monde has reported, external that police have continued to use a different model in subsequent protests. Protests also took place in Italy, with some clashes between police and demonstrators in Rome and Turin. In Portugal, police moved to clear a new tent camp that had been assembled after thousands marched to protest against a rental bill that they argue could worsen a housing crisis in the country, where house prices have more than doubled over the past decade. Mostly young protesters have recently taken to the streets in a swathe of European nations: France, Belgium, Ireland, Spain, Portugal, Italy, Greece, Serbia and Albania. While the specific demands vary from country to country, the protesters have largely focused on cost-of-living issues, such as access to housing, the quality of education and cuts to public services. articles.summaryTr: The crypto exchange said it has begun phased withdrawals after the record hack the FBI has blamed on North Korea.
articles.articleText: Binance says phase one of withdrawals opens after $6.3B hack The crypto exchange said it has begun phased withdrawals after the record hack the FBI has blamed on North Korea. Binance said it has reopened its Bitcoin network in phase one of resuming withdrawals after a major hack of about $6.3 billion in funds. The crypto exchange had suspended user withdrawals after the attack on Thursday, which the FBI blamed on North Korean operatives. “First batch network now opened in phase one of withdrawals is $BTC bitcoin network,” Binance said on X. In an earlier X announcement on Sunday, Binance had said it would roll out withdrawal services in phases, which will be progressively available. Updates will be available on its official X channel, it added. “We are taking a phased approach by prioritizing tokens based on the past week data of user demand, so that each network and asset pair can be restored carefully, with stability and security checks completed before access is reopened,” Binance said. Users should check the withdrawal page for their selected asset and network, or visit the Binance network status page to confirm availability, the company said. During the phased rollout, it is expected that there will be some congestion, longer processing times and even temporary delays, Binance said, so if a withdrawal is not successful, users should try again after a short while. Cointelegraph reported on Saturday that Binance said it had replenished 90% of the assets stolen in the hack, up from 80% a day earlier, and remained on track to resume withdrawals Sunday. Magazine: Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen

It expects these assets to be further converted, using DeFi and instant swap services, as the hackers move to more advanced laundering stages. The FBI urged private sector entities including THORNode operators, RPC node operators, instant exchanges, DeFi services, blockchain analytics firms and other digital asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets. A full list of addresses is provided on the news release. Cointelegraph reported earlier this year that North Korea-linked hackers stole about 60% of the value lost to crypto hacks in 2025, with proceeds used to help fund the regime’s nuclear and ballistic missile programs, highlighting a growing reliance on digital assets to generate hard currency. North Korean defense spending supplemented Related: Crypto losses from North Korea hackers in 2025 rose 51% YoY: Report Those findings came from a CertiK report that attributed more than $2 billion of an estimated $3.4 billion in 2025 crypto security losses to groups tied North Korea, across 79 of 656 incidents documented that year. While North Korea does not publish credible budget data, according to independent research organization MilitarySpend, mid-range consensus places its actual annual defense spending at as much as $6 billion, using purchasing-power-adjusted GDP estimates, though this figure is uncertain. MilitarySpend adds that revenue from Russia arms transfers — estimated at as much as $5 billion in munitions exported to Russia from 2022-2025 per South Korean intelligence — supplements domestic weapons programs, as does cryptocurrency theft, which provides additional off-budget financing for WMD development. As Cointelegraph reported, between 2016 and early 2026, North Korea-linked actors stole an estimated $6.75 billion in cryptocurrency across 263 documented incidents, according to CertiK, citing findings by independent onchain researcher Taylor Monahan. CertiK’s analysis concluded that North Korea has industrialized crypto theft into a core state revenue mechanism. Magazine: Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen

articles.title: Energy bills help 'doesn't go far enough'
articles.summary: Families in the West Midlands say they are worried about paying winter energy bills.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Energy bills help 'doesn't go far enough'
articles.summaryTr: Families in the West Midlands say they are worried about paying winter energy bills.
articles.articleText: Energy bills help 'doesn't go far enough' - Published Households in the West Midlands said they want to see the government revisit energy bills in the wake of the Budget - amid concerns the help being offered won't go far enough. Chancellor John Healey announced a £100 'household energy payment', and a future plan to remove gas standing charges, as part of a wider package to address the cost of living. Families in the region told the BBC they were "grateful" for the assistance, but were concerned about their finances over the winter. Kelly Birkett, a personal accountant from Redditch, said: "The £100 is good, but it's not great. It just gets absorbed into everything else families have to pay for, just to get by." Birkett, a married mum-of-two, said her family was already considering what to cut back on in the wake of the Budget. "I know I sound a little but ungrateful for the £100, and I don't want to be. I'm certainly not ungrateful," she said. "But in reality we're no better off. With the temperatures dropping we know the heating will have to be on, the children can't be cold. "We'll dig deep to make sure we're a little more conservative when it comes to the heating, but for sure it's something most families will be worried about (the winter.)" Mark Sumner, a coach driver from Alcester, said him and his wife sold their previous home partly to clear old debts that had accrued from bills including energy. He told the BBC they had fallen into "energy debt" and were concerned about this coming winter. "We know our bill will go up again, you're just dreading it each time the increase comes around, as to how much it will be," he said. "I very rarely take our children out for anything to eat anymore, and we're very careful about what we spend at the shops. "What the government has announced is helpful. I don't want to be ungrateful so I will say it's helpful for us, but it probably only covers one month (of bills). "So it's a slight help, but it's not enough." 'We are being fair to families' The government said "millions of families" would benefit from the measures announced in the Budget, including freezing fuel duty, the 3.9% minimum wage increase and scrapping plans to reduce the £20,000 tax-free limit on ISAs. Chancellor John Healey said the energy announcement was "just a small part" of what the government was doing to help families. "Conflict in the Middle East and Europe is hitting families here at home through higher everyday costs," he said. "We can't control global events, but we can act where we can make a difference." There is no definitive date for scrapping the standing charge on gas, but the Treasury has committed to doing it either in 2027 or "as soon as possible after". The VAT cut on electricity bills, which was due to end in April, will be extended to July next year. articles.title: Diwali hampers to bring hope to families in need
articles.summary: The Diwali Basket Brigade volunteers want to help vulnerable households with rising food prices.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Diwali hampers to bring hope to families in need
articles.summaryTr: The Diwali Basket Brigade volunteers want to help vulnerable households with rising food prices.
articles.articleText: Diwali hampers to bring hope to families in need - Published Hundreds of volunteers have packed food parcels to distribute to people across Birmingham struggling with the rising cost of living. About 300 people turned up to the Diwali Basket Brigade event at the RSRS Centre in Hockley, which was organised by The Diwali Foundation. It is the ninth time the charity has brought community volunteers from a variety of backgrounds together to make hampers in the build up to the religious festival. Deepak Parekh, founder of the initiative, said: "[The] cost of living crisis hasn't gone away... but Diwali is a celebration of light over darkness, and this is our little way of bringing some light and some hope into the families that need it most." The Diwali Foundation, who are based in Herefordshire, said that more than 12% of UK households are experiencing food poverty. It works with about forty different food banks and charities to reach vulnerable households. To date, the charity said it has provided around 23,470 food hampers to those in need. Volunteer Clare Hannah said, while packing bags: "You're thinking about, 'oh I wonder what they're going to make with this'. And the fact that this is all that they've got, for some people." Parcels were taken from Hockley to residents living in homes provided by Walsall Housing Group (whg). Faye Shanahan from whg said: "It's really tough out there. Our customers are having a really hard time. The cost of living is not easing. "Events like this today are really, really fantastic. It makes an absolutely fantastic difference to our customers." Resident John Whiting, who turned 80 on Saturday, described his parcel as "unbelievable". "There are a lot of people out there that've got nothing," he added. "The food will be tremendous, thank you." A London event was also held on Saturday, with similar events in Manchester and Leicester planned for Sunday. Organisers have set a target of providing 6,000 food hampers this year, which would top a 2025 record when more than 80,000 meals were provided. articles.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

articles.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
articles.articleText: Release Number 9316-26 CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced the CFTC’s plan to increase the publication frequency of the Commitments of Traders Report (COT Report) from once to twice a week by the end of 2026. Data from Monday will be published on Wednesday, and data from Wednesday will be published on Friday. Both reports will be released at 3:30 p.m. ET on their respective publication days. Under the enhanced publication schedule, the reports’ latency will decrease from three days to two days. The change follows the Commission’s recent Request for Comment and reflects its commitment to providing market participants with more timely information about trading positions and activity in agricultural markets. The CFTC’s Division of Data is leading the effort to operationalize the expanded publication schedule through modernization and automation while maintaining accuracy. “COT Reports have been an important source of transparency for decades. Following feedback from the agricultural community, I’m pleased to announce the CFTC will be rolling out COT Reports twice a week to ensure this information stream is as useful as possible,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
articles.articleText: Release Number 9315-26 CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced today it has filed a lawsuit against Utah to block the state’s efforts to shut down CFTC-registered contract markets using state laws. The lawsuit follows Utah’s decision to file civil enforcement actions in state court against CFTC-regulated markets and other businesses. Utah’s effort to restrict the functioning of CFTC-registered exchanges obstructs Congress’s decision to federally preempt state law. “Utah seeks to shut down prediction markets across a wide variety of markets,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Event contracts do not just serve hedging and investment purposes—they also provide the public with information about the outcome of future events. Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets. As I’ve said before, the CFTC has the expertise and responsibility to defend its exclusive jurisdiction over commodity derivatives, and that’s exactly what we’ll do.” This action reflects the CFTC’s firm commitment to maintaining its exclusive jurisdiction over CFTC-registered prediction markets. The CFTC continues to draw a clear line: if a state challenges the lawful operation of a derivatives exchange, the Commission will protect federal sovereign interests. The Commission has also initiated legal proceedings against nine other states and has submitted briefs in four federal courts of appeal and one state supreme court. -CFTC-
articles.articleTextTr: Release Number 9315-26 CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced today it has filed a lawsuit against Utah to block the state’s efforts to shut down CFTC-registered contract markets using state laws. The lawsuit follows Utah’s decision to file civil enforcement actions in state court against CFTC-regulated markets and other businesses. Utah’s effort to restrict the functioning of CFTC-registered exchanges obstructs Congress’s decision to federally preempt state law. “Utah seeks to shut down prediction markets across a wide variety of markets,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Event contracts do not just serve hedging and investment purposes—they also provide the public with information about the outcome of future events. Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets. As I’ve said before, the CFTC has the expertise and responsibility to defend its exclusive jurisdiction over commodity derivatives, and that’s exactly what we’ll do.” This action reflects the CFTC’s firm commitment to maintaining its exclusive jurisdiction over CFTC-registered prediction markets. The CFTC continues to draw a clear line: if a state challenges the lawful operation of a derivatives exchange, the Commission will protect federal sovereign interests. The Commission has also initiated legal proceedings against nine other states and has submitted briefs in four federal courts of appeal and one state supreme court. -CFTC-

Through the MOU, the CFTC and NBA will better share information by regularly communicating and discussing matters relating to integrity, as well as maintaining fair and transparent prediction markets. “I’m pleased the CFTC and NBA signed an MOU which continues the Commission’s commitment to increasing data sharing between the agency and professional sports leagues,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. articles.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Louisiana Man and His Companies to Pay Over $9 Million in Forex Fraud
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Louisiana Man and His Companies to Pay Over $9 Million in Forex Fraud
articles.articleText: Release Number 9313-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Louisiana Man and His Companies to Pay Over $9 Million in Forex Fraud October 21, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana entered a default judgment against defendants Michael B. DePetrillo, Meteor LLC, and NOLA FX Capital Management LLC for their participation in a fraudulent retail forex scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented that participant funds would be used to trade retail forex, made material misrepresentations and omissions regarding the profitability of forex trading with them, and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying DePetrillo’s personal expenses, and trading in DePetrillo’s personal account. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,211,492 civil monetary penalty. The order also permanently enjoins the defendants from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposes permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2024 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9003-24] On Feb. 18, 2025, in a related criminal case, DePetrillo pleaded guilty to violating the Commodity Exchange Act in connection with the same conduct in the CFTC’s complaint. On July 23, 2025, the court sentenced him to nine years in prison and ordered him to pay $6,748,412 in restitution. The CFTC appreciates the assistance of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Louisiana and the FBI New Orleans Division. -CFTC-

news.title: Democrat endorses Republican candidate in key Michigan Senate race as party spat escalates
news.summary: Haley Stevens, who lost out on the Democratic Senate nomination to Abdul El-Sayed, endorses his opponent days before the vote.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Democrat endorses Republican candidate in key Michigan Senate race as party spat escalates
news.summaryTr: Haley Stevens, who lost out on the Democratic Senate nomination to Abdul El-Sayed, endorses his opponent days before the vote.
news.articleText: Democrat endorses Republican candidate in key Michigan Senate race as party spat escalates - Published A Democrat in Michigan has endorsed the Republican candidate in the state's crucial US Senate contest, as a spat with her own party's candidate Abdul El-Sayed escalated just days before the vote. Haley Stevens, a sitting congresswoman who lost out on the Democratic Senate nomination to El-Sayed, made a surprise appearance alongside the Republican candidate Mike Rogers at a church on Sunday. "I don't belong in Abdul's campaign," she said in a video posted to X shortly after that appearance. "Who we are as Michiganders is not hate and is not what we are getting out from our Democratic nominee right now." "That's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers," Stevens said. Stevens also said El-Sayed had apparently told her she was no longer welcome in his campaign. "This is a very close election, we all know that, but Abdul made clear that I was not welcome in his campaign, that he didn't need me there, that he didn't want me there," Stevens told reporters after the Sunday church service. The pair had been scheduled to appear together at a different event on Sunday, but El-Sayed reportedly asked her not to come. They had clashed publicly over a campaign advert from an outside liberal group which blamed Israel for high food prices. El-Sayed criticised the advert and said he had nothing to do with its contents. When asked about Stevens' endorsement, El-Sayed told reporters he was focused on the problems Michiganders are facing. "At the end of the day, I don't think about Haley Stevens," he said. "None of this matters." In downtown Detroit, people were grabbing lunch or making their way to Ford Field stadium for the Detroit Lions American football game when the news broke. Every democrat that the BBC spoke with shared that they were disappointed by her endorsement of Rogers. Summer Lawrence, a 21-year-old student, told the BBC that Stevens' endorsement felt like a betrayal to the Democratic party and everything she told voters she stood for. "I just genuinely don't understand it," she said. "I do think it's a betrayal of the party because the things she stands for are not the same things that he stands for as a Republican." Matthew Barera, another Michigan voter told the BBC, he, too, did not understand Stevens' reasoning. "I don't know if she had her own revenge or not, maybe she had frustrations with the party in her own elections," he said. Others, including Republicans who support Rogers, said they doubted it would make a difference to the race. "People can see right through her actions, you know? She's just angry," Marissa Lee, a Rogers supporter, told the BBC. "She is not going to make anybody change their mind." The Michigan Senate race is considered by analysts to be one of the tightest in Tuesday's midterm elections, which will decide which party controls Congress for the next two years. It is one of a handful of battleground contests that will ultimately decide control of the Senate. The seat is currently held by a retiring Democrat and the last time a Republican was elected to this Senate seat was in 1994. But in presidential elections, it is one of the crucial swing states - Michigan voted for Democrat Joe Biden in 2020 but Trump in 2024. Rogers welcomed Stevens' endorsement and said it showed "courage" during brief remarks with reporters outside the church. President Donald Trump echoed that sentiment saying on Truth Social that, "[Stevens] showed great and almost unprecedented loyalty to the Great People of Michigan with what she did". Many of Stevens' staff reportedly resigned immediately after her announcement, while the chair of the Democratic Party in Michigan said her decision "shows that she has abandoned everything she claims to care about". "We reject the attempts by Stevens and bad-faith actors to divide our party and undermine our momentum," Curtis Hertel said in a statement. Over the weekend, as Stevens' criticism of El-Sayed escalated, a number of Democratic politicians in Michigan publicly encouraged her to end the feud and back the party's candidates more directly. "It feels like it's more about her feelings than Michiganders," State Senator Mallory McMorrow said on MSNow. "It is a choice between MAGA and Michigan. And I'm on team Michigan." On Sunday, Democratic Senator Chuck Schumer called Stevens' endorsement of Rogers "a despicable betrayal" of her political party. "Senate Democrats are united in our support for Abdul El-Sayed, because we know he will fight for the economic interests of working families in Michigan, unlike Mike Rogers, who is a tool of Donald Trump and billionaire donors," Schumer said. After a bruising and sometimes bitter campaign earlier this year, El-Sayed, a left-wing outsider, defeated Stevens, the establishment-backed congresswoman, to win the party's nomination for the US Senate race. The primary, and the pair's subsequent feud, has underlined divisions over the party's direction ahead of the 2028 presidential election. Former public health official El-Sayed, who is the son of Egyptian immigrants, has channelled grassroots frustration with Washington politics as well as US ties to Israel. Stevens is a more centrist Democrat - and had the support of party figures such as Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer during the primary race. Follow the twists and turns of Trump's second term with North America correspondent Anthony Zurcher's US Politics Unspun newsletter. Readers in the UK can sign up here. news.title: Anthropic'ten yapay zekaya oyun freni: Claude artık yeniden oluşturamayacak
news.summary: Anthropic’in Claude Code aracına, yapay zekânın mevcut video oyunlarını yeniden oluşturmasını engelleyen yeni bir talimat eklediği ortaya çıktı. XDA Developers’ın incelemesine göre kısıtlama, özellikle Opus 5.5 modelinde aktif.

news.titleTr: Anthropic'ten yapay zekaya oyun freni: Claude artık yeniden oluşturamayacak
news.summaryTr: Anthropic’in Claude Code aracına, yapay zekânın mevcut video oyunlarını yeniden oluşturmasını engelleyen yeni bir talimat eklediği ortaya çıktı. XDA Developers’ın incelemesine göre kısıtlama, özellikle Opus 5.5 modelinde aktif.
news.articleText: Anthropic'ten yapay zekaya oyun freni: Claude artık yeniden oluşturamayacak - Anthropic'in Claude Code aracına, yapay zekanın mevcut video oyunlarını yeniden oluşturmasını engelleyen yeni bir talimat eklediği ortaya çıktı. XDA Developers'ın incelemesine göre kısıtlama, özellikle Opus 5.5 modelinde aktif. - Düzenlemenin oyun portları ve tersine mühendislik projelerini nasıl etkileyeceği ise belirsizliğini koruyor. Yapay zeka destekli oyun geliştirme projelerine yönelik yeni bir kısıtlama gündeme geldi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Anthropic'in kodlama aracı Claude Code'a, yapay zeka modellerinin mevcut bir video oyununun aynısını yeniden oluşturmasını engelleyen bir talimat eklediği bildirildi. XDA Developers'ın haberine göre söz konusu talimat, belirli bir oyunun ismi değiştirilerek veya özgün bir proje gibi sunularak yeniden oluşturulmasını da kapsıyor. Talimatın, Anthropic sunucularından Claude Code’a iletilen bir yapılandırma üzerinden uygulandığı belirtildi. Claude Code'un sisteminde yeni talimat bulundu Söz konusu kısıtlama ilk olarak X platformunda bir kullanıcı ve YouTuber tarafından paylaşıldı. XDA Developers ise talimatı Claude Code’un 2.1.314 sürümündeki yazılım dosyalarında bağımsız olarak doğruladığını açıkladı. Talimatın içeriğinde, Claude’un özgün oyunlar, belirli bir türden esinlenen yapımlar ve kullanıcıların kendi tasarım ve varlıklarıyla oluşturduğu projelere yardımcı olabileceği belirtiliyor. Buna karşılık, adı değiştirilse veya özgün olduğu iddia edilse bile mevcut bir oyunun yeniden oluşturulmasına destek verilmemesi isteniyor. XDA’nın incelemesi, kısıtlamanın Opus 5.5 modeline ayrı bir mekanizma üzerinden de iletilebildiğini ortaya koydu. Ancak düzenlemenin tüm kullanıcılara ve modellere ne ölçüde yayıldığı henüz net değil. Pokémon ve Zelda projeleri etkilenebilir XDA’nın yaptığı testlerde Claude Opus 5.5, Pokémon Diamond oyununun yeniden oluşturulmasına yönelik talepleri reddetti. Model, mevcut bir oyunun yeniden yaratılmasının oturum talimatlarıyla yasaklandığını belirtti. Buna karşılık, oyunun kodlarının incelenmesi ve tersine mühendislik çalışmaları konusunda farklı yanıtlar verdi. Opus 5.5, decompile işlemlerine yardımcı olabileceğini, ayrıştırılmış kodları daha okunabilir hale getirebileceğini ve kullanıcının kendi oyun kopyası üzerinden yeniden derleme araçları geliştirebileceğini ifade etti. Bu ayrım, özellikle eski oyunları farklı platformlarda çalıştırmayı amaçlayan projeler açısından önem taşıyor. Zelda: Wind Waker HD gibi oyunların bilgisayarlara taşınmasını sağlayan statik yeniden derleme projeleri ile Nintendo Switch oyunlarını Mac üzerinde çalıştırmayı hedefleyen uyumluluk araçlarının yeni kısıtlamadan nasıl etkileneceği belirsiz. Oyun geliştiricilerinden kısıtlama tepkisi XDA'nın aktardığına göre bir geliştirici, 30 Ekim’de Anthropic'in GitHub sayfasında Claude'un ücretli müşteriler için hazırladığı dijital masa ve savaş oyunu modüllerine yardımcı olmayı reddettiğini bildirdi. Geliştirici, projelerin müşterilerin sahip olduğu fiziksel oyunlardan ve sağladıkları materyallerden hareketle kişiselleştirildiğini belirtti. Anthropic’in kısıtlamayı ne kadar geniş uygulayacağına ilişkin henüz net bir açıklaması bulunmuyor. Şirketin oyun portları, decompile ve yeniden derleme projelerine yaklaşımı konusunda XDA’nın yönelttiği sorulara da haberin yayımlandığı sırada yanıt verilmediği aktarıldı. news.title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire to end
news.summary: A rare humanitarian ceasefire has allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire to end
news.summaryTr: A rare humanitarian ceasefire has allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.
news.articleText: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire to end - Published A rare humanitarian ceasefire in Ukraine's Kherson region, that has allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, is due to end on Sunday night. While the localised ceasefire on the front line has held since it was implemented last week, fighting has continued elsewhere. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had struck energy infrastructure in four regions overnight on Saturday, leaving hundreds of thousands of homes without power. Another overnight strike killed two people, including a 13-year-old girl, in the Vinnytsia region, the State Emergency Service of Ukraine said. Meanwhile, Ukraine hit a major missile fuel producer in Russia's Rostov region, which caused a fire and damaged four production facilities, Zelensky said. In Ukraine, repair works to restore power continued throughout the day. Most customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region had their connections restored by early evening, but more than 60,000 were still without power, the governor said. Because of regular attacks on energy infrastructure, emergency power cuts have been introduced across the country. Even in the capital Kyiv, electricity is cut off for most of the day, and water supplies are also disrupted. Zelensky said in a social media post that the intensity of Russian strikes has been "extremely high" over the past week, adding that Russia was "trying to take maximum advantage of the shortage of ballistic missile interceptors". He added that "every day" Ukraine communicated its need for Patriot missiles - the only effective weapon for downing Russia's deadly ballistic missiles - to the US, Europe and other partners. He thanked countries for their support so far and longer-term commitments, but called again for more immediate aid. On the front line, a localised ceasefire in the Kherson region was due to end at 22:59 Ukrainian time (21:00 GMT) on Sunday. The limited pause in hostilities, which started on Tuesday, was brokered with the help of US First Lady Melania Trump and Pope Leo. It was originally confined to the city of Oleshky, which has been occupied by Russia since the first days of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and was expanded across the wider region of Kherson. Oleshky had been trapped on one side by the Dnipro river and the other by Russian forces, with routes out mined and subject to drone attack. Residents trapped there were suffering severe shortages of food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive. The truce allowed for Oleskhy residents to evacuate if they wanted, and there were emotional scenes on Saturday of reunions between loved ones who hadn't seen eachother for years. There are Ukrainian military positions just 5km (3.1 miles) from Oleshky, but evacuees had to travel through Russian-occupied territory to southern Russia, where they flew to Belarus, before finally being driven across Ukraine's northern border. The oldest evacuee was 94 years old, while the youngest was one, according to Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's human rights ombudsman. Related topics - Published1 day ago

news.titleTr: Putin ile Zelenskiy masaya oturacak mı? Kremlin’den açıklama
news.summaryTr: Kremlin Dış Politika Danışmanı Yuriy Uşakov, Ukrayna Devlet Başkanı Volodimir Zelenskiy’nin araması halinde Rusya Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin’in görüşmeye hazır olduğunu söyledi. Uşakov, Putin’in görüşmekten hiçbir zaman vazgeçmediğini belirtti.
news.articleText: Putin ile Zelenskiy masaya oturacak mı? Kremlin’den açıklama - Kremlin Dış Politika Danışmanı Yuriy Uşakov, Ukrayna Devlet Başkanı Volodimir Zelenskiy’nin araması halinde Rusya Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin’in görüşmeye hazır olduğunu söyledi. - Uşakov, Putin’in görüşmekten hiçbir zaman vazgeçmediğini belirtti. Kremlin’den Ukrayna ile olası müzakerelere ilişkin dikkat çeken bir açıklama geldi. Rusya Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin’in Dış Politika Danışmanı Yuriy Uşakov, Ukrayna Devlet Başkanı Volodimir Zelenskiy’nin telefon etmesi halinde Putin’in çağrıyı yanıtlayacağını söyledi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Rus televizyon kanalı Rossiya’ya konuşan Uşakov, Ukrayna krizinin çözümüne yönelik diplomatik temasları değerlendirdi. “Buyursun gelsin” Zelenskiy’nin Putin ile Moskova’da görüşebileceğini belirten Uşakov, Ukrayna liderinin farklı kanallar üzerinden görüşme isteğine ilişkin sinyaller gönderdiğini ifade etti. Uşakov, "Madem bu kadar görüşmek istiyor, buyursun gelsin." dedi. Zelenskiy’nin Putin’i araması halinde Rus liderin telefonu açıp açmayacağı sorusunu da yanıtlayan Uşakov, “Putin'in açacağını düşünüyorum. Putin, hiçbir zaman görüşmekten vazgeçmedi” ifadelerini kullandı. Abu Dabi’de üçlü müzakere mesajı Uşakov, Ukrayna konusunda Birleşik Arap Emirlikleri’nin başkenti Abu Dabi’de yapılması planlanan üçlü müzakerelere Avrupalı temsilcilerin katılması ihtimalini de değerlendirdi. ABD ile çalışma düzeyinde temasların sürdüğünü belirten Uşakov, bu nedenle müzakerelerin ilk turlarının üçlü formatta gerçekleştirilmesinin mantıklı olduğunu söyledi. Rusya, Ukrayna ve ABD arasında yürütülmesi planlanan üçlü görüşmeler, savaşın sona erdirilmesine yönelik diplomatik girişimlerin önemli başlıklarından biri olarak öne çıkıyor.

news.titleTr: Peaceful protests in Germany spiral into violence and looting
news.summaryTr: Thousands joined largely orderly demonstrations earlier in the day, before violence erupted in Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg.
news.articleText: Peaceful protests in Germany spiral into violence and looting Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday as clashes erupted in German cities over the cost of living. The rallies were organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt - meaning "Gen Z takes charge". Thousands had taken part in the largely peaceful demonstrations across Germany before violence broke out. At least 54 people were arrested in Frankfurt and over 100 police officers left injured, according to German authorities. Besides Frankfurt - Germany's financial hub - there were outbreaks of violence in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg. This comes as protests have been taking place across Europe over the rising cost of living, poor public services, and a lack of affordable housing. The BBC's world correspondent Joe Inwood reports.

news.titleTr: 31 yaşındaki kadının ölümünde ChatGPT iddiası: Aile hukuk mücadelesi başlattı
news.summaryTr: ABD’de yaşayan 31 yaşındaki yazılım mühendisi Bowen Wan, epilepsi tedavisinde kullandığı ilacın dozunu ChatGPT’nin önerileri doğrultusunda azalttıktan sonra hayatını kaybetti.
news.articleText: 31 yaşındaki kadının ölümünde ChatGPT iddiası: Aile hukuk mücadelesi başlattı - ABD'de yaşayan 31 yaşındaki yazılım mühendisi Bowen Wan, epilepsi tedavisinde kullandığı ilacın dozunu ChatGPT'nin önerileri doğrultusunda azalttıktan sonra hayatını kaybetti. - Ailesi, sohbet robotunun doktor kontrolünü devre dışı bırakan tavsiyelerde bulunduğunu öne sürerek OpenAI ve CEO’su Sam Altman’a dava açtı. ABD'de yaşayan 31 yaşındaki yazılım mühendisi Bowen Wan'ın ölümü, yapay zeka araçlarının sağlık konularındaki rolünü yeniden gündeme taşıdı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Ailesinin açtığı davaya dayanan New York Times haberine göre Wan, epilepsi tedavisinde kullandığı ilacın dozunu ChatGPT ile yaptığı görüşmelerin ardından kendi başına azaltmaya başladı. Wan, şubat ayında Seattle'daki evinde ölü bulundu. Ölümünün, epilepsiye bağlı ani beklenmedik ölüm (SUDEP) komplikasyonundan kaynaklandığı belirtildi. Ailesi, genç kadının ölümünden önceki günlerde ChatGPT’den ilaç dozunu nasıl azaltabileceğine ilişkin tavsiyeler aldığını ileri sürdü. ChatGPT ile kurduğu ilişki zamanla yoğunlaştı 2021 yılında epilepsi nöbetleri sıklaşan Wan, Amazon'daki yazılım mühendisliği görevinden sağlık sorunları nedeniyle izin aldı. Sosyal hayattan giderek uzaklaşan Wan, 2023 yılında ChatGPT2yi ilişki tavsiyeleri almak ve sigorta ile engellilik yardımları gibi konularda destek almak için kullanmaya başladı. Ailesinin aktardığına göre 2025 yılına gelindiğinde chatbot ile haftada ortalama 1.500 mesajlaşıyordu. Aynı dönemde ailesiyle daha az iletişim kurmaya başladı. Wan, Mart 2025'te ChatGPT'ye yazdığı bir mesajda, sohbet ederken onu bir arkadaş gibi görmeye başladığını ifade etti. İlaç dozunu azaltma süreci Habere göre Wan, Amazon’daki işinden çıkarılmasının ardından yeni bir iş bulabilmek için bilişsel becerilerini ve konuşma yeteneğini etkilediğini düşündüğü ilaçların dozunu azaltmayı değerlendirdi. Ocak 2026'da epilepsi ilacının günlük dozunu 400 miligramdan önce 300, ardından 200 miligrama indirmek için ChatGPT'den tavsiye istedi. Chatbot başlangıçta doktora danışmasını önerse de daha sonraki görüşmelerde Wan'ı doktor reçetesine bağlı kalmama konusunda desteklediği iddia edildi. Wan'ın babası Qun Wan, kızının ChatGPT ile yaptığı görüşmelerde ilacın dozunu birkaç hafta içinde tamamen sıfırlamaya yönelik bir plan oluşturduğunu sonradan öğrendi. İlaç dozunun düşürülmesiyle birlikte Wan’da kafa karışıklığı ve hafıza sorunları gibi belirtiler ortaya çıktı. Ailenin dava dosyasına göre genç kadın, yaşadığı sorunlarla ilgili toplam 158 kez endişesini dile getirdi. Ancak chatbotun bu belirtileri önemsemeyerek beyninin "düşük güç modunda" olduğu yönünde yanıtlar verdiği öne sürüldü. Wan’ın son mesajını, cesedinin bulunmasından üç gün önce gönderdiği belirtildi. Aile OpenAI ve Sam Altman’a dava açtı Wan ailesi, OpenAI ve şirketin CEO'su Sam Altman'a karşı haksız ölüm davası açtı. Ailenin avukatları, ChatGPT'nin lisansı olmadan tıbbi tavsiyelerde bulunduğunu ve doktorları danışılması gereken uzmanlar yerine aşılması gereken engeller gibi gösterdiğini savundu. OpenAI sözcüsü Drew Pusateri ise New York Times'a yaptığı açıklamada olayın son derece üzücü olduğunu belirtti. Pusateri, Wan'ın kullandığı GPT-4o modelinin artık kullanılamadığını ve ChatGPT'nin tıbbi bakımın yerini tutmadığını vurguladı. Wan, şubat ayında Seattle'daki evinde ölü bulundu. Ölümünün, epilepsiye bağlı ani beklenmedik ölüm (SUDEP) komplikasyonundan kaynaklandığı belirtildi. ChatGPT ile kurduğu ilişki zamanla yoğunlaştı 2021 yılında epilepsi nöbetleri sıklaşan Wan, Amazon'daki yazılım mühendisliği görevinden sağlık sorunları nedeniyle izin aldı. Ailesinin aktardığına göre 2025 yılına gelindiğinde chatbot ile haftada ortalama 1.500 mesajlaşıyordu. Aynı dönemde ailesiyle daha az iletişim kurmaya başladı. news.summary: Fenerbahçe Spor Kulübü, Başkan Aziz Yıldırım ve bazı yöneticiler hakkında ortaya atılan yönetim krizi iddialarına ilişkin açıklama yaptı. Sarı lacivertli kulüp, söz konusu haberlerin gerçeği yansıtmadığını bildirdi.

news.titleTr: Fenerbahçe'den yönetim krizi iddialarına yanıt: "Tamamen gerçek dışı"
news.summaryTr: Fenerbahçe Spor Kulübü, Başkan Aziz Yıldırım ve bazı yöneticiler hakkında ortaya atılan yönetim krizi iddialarına ilişkin açıklama yaptı. Sarı lacivertli kulüp, söz konusu haberlerin gerçeği yansıtmadığını bildirdi.
news.articleText: Fenerbahçe'den yönetim krizi iddialarına yanıt: "Tamamen gerçek dışı" - Fenerbahçe Kulübü, Aziz Yıldırım ve yöneticiler hakkında ortaya atılan Barcelona seyahati ve yönetim krizi iddialarını yalanladı. - Kulüp, yöneticilerin tarifeli uçakla Barcelona-Real Madrid maçını izlediğini belirterek istifa iddialarının gerçeği yansıtmadığını açıkladı. Fenerbahçe Kulübü, Başkan Aziz Yıldırım ve bazı yöneticiler hakkında gündeme gelen yönetim krizi iddialarına ilişkin açıklama yaptı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Kulüp, Elis Buse Araç tarafından paylaşılan iddiaların tamamen gerçek dışı olduğunu bildirdi. Kulübün açıklamasında, yöneticiler Batuhan Özdemir ve Savaş Adalet'in tarifeli uçakla seyahat ederek Barcelona-Real Madrid karşılaşmasını yerinde takip ettiği belirtildi. Haberde adı geçen Ömer Onan'ın ise son iki yıldır Barcelona'ya gitmediği ifade edildi. İstifa iddialarına yalanlama Açıklamada, Aziz Yıldırım'ın yöneticilere futbol takımıyla ilgili herhangi bir görev verdiği, Barcelona seyahati nedeniyle tepki gösterdiği veya istifalarını istediği yönündeki iddiaların gerçeği yansıtmadığı vurgulandı. Haberde aktarılan konuşmaların yaşanmadığı ve iddia edildiği gibi bir yönetim krizinin bulunmadığı kaydedildi. Fenerbahçe yönetimi, kulübün hassas bir dönemden geçtiğine dikkat çekerek yönetim içinde ayrışma olduğu algısı yaratmaya yönelik asılsız haberlere itibar edilmemesi çağrısında bulundu.

news.title: Armed police start patrols in Sydney after Bondi Beach attack
news.summary: The new police unit is a security measure in response to last year's deadly shooting attack at a Hanukkah festival.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Armed police start patrols in Sydney after Bondi Beach attack
news.summaryTr: The new police unit is a security measure in response to last year's deadly shooting attack at a Hanukkah festival.
news.articleText: Armed police start patrols in Sydney after Bondi Beach attack - Published Heavily-armed police officers have started patrolling Sydney's streets, as part of heightened security measures following last year's deadly shooting at Bondi Beach. The Armed Response Command (ARC) will see specially trained officers in busy tourist areas carrying long-arm rifles – an unfamiliar sight for most residents. New South Wales police say the officers will also patrol major events like sports matches and places of worship "to prevent, deter and rapidly respond to serious threats, including active armed offender incidents". Fifteen people - including a 10-year-old girl – were killed in December when two gunmen opened fire on an event marking the Jewish festival of Hanukkah at the popular beach. The attack was Australia's worst mass shooting in almost three decades and prompted sweeping gun law reforms and a crackdown on hate speech. One resident told ABC news that the sight of armed police was "unnerving". "They are just everywhere. Those guns are huge." But another woman told the broadcaster that seeing police with weapons made her feel safe. ARC is specifically designed to be "highly visible across Sydney, driving specialist vehicles and carrying rifles," New South Wales police said in a statement. Its role "is built on a simple principle - preserving life," Detective Superintendent Andrew Evans said. The shooting on 14 December put huge pressure on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's government, with calls for immediate action on antisemitism. Jewish communities have welcomed the new police operation, which will eventually consist of 250 officers, but others have called for safeguards to protect human rights. "No Australian wants to see officers with military weapons on our streets, but the sight of body bags is far worse," Alex Ryvchin, co-CEO of Executive Council of Australian Jewry, said. But Amnesty International Australia said it was concerned about the "militarisation of policing", and asked for assurances from the state government that ARC will not be used to suppress peaceful protests. "Any expansion of police powers and capabilities must be accompanied by clear, publicly accessible rules, robust independent oversight and accountability," said the organisation's Andrew Witheford. The New South Wales administration defended the new measures. "Our world changed forever. That's just the truth of it, right across this country. And I said it at the time, we will never be the same again," the state's Police Minister Yasmin Catley told the ABC. One of the alleged gunmen, Naveed Akram, has been charged with 78 offences including 15 counts of murder, 40 counts of attempted murder, and one count of committing a terrorist act. His father, Sajid Akram, 50 - who was also armed and shot at the crowd on Bondi Beach - was killed by police at the scene. - Published18 December 2025 - Published14 December 2025

news.summary: ABD Başkanı Donald Trump ile Kanada Başbakanı Mark Carney, iki ülke arasında uzun süredir devam eden ticaret anlaşmazlıklarını telefonda görüştü. Carney, görüşmenin yapıcı geçtiğini belirtirken, ekiplerin önümüzdeki haftalarda anlaşma için çalışacağını açıkladı.

news.titleTr: Trump ve Carney arasında kritik telefon görüşmesi: Ticaret anlaşmasında yeni adım
news.summaryTr: ABD Başkanı Donald Trump ile Kanada Başbakanı Mark Carney, iki ülke arasında uzun süredir devam eden ticaret anlaşmazlıklarını telefonda görüştü. Carney, görüşmenin yapıcı geçtiğini belirtirken, ekiplerin önümüzdeki haftalarda anlaşma için çalışacağını açıkladı.
news.articleText: Trump ve Carney arasında kritik telefon görüşmesi: Ticaret anlaşmasında yeni adım - ABD Başkanı Donald Trump ile Kanada Başbakanı Mark Carney, iki ülke arasında uzun süredir devam eden ticaret anlaşmazlıklarını telefonda görüştü. - Carney, görüşmenin yapıcı geçtiğini belirtirken, ekiplerin önümüzdeki haftalarda anlaşma için çalışacağını açıkladı. ABD ile Kanada arasındaki ticaret geriliminde diplomatik temaslar hız kazandı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Kanada Başbakanı Mark Carney ile ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, iki ülke arasındaki ticaret ilişkilerinin geleceğini ele almak üzere telefonda görüştü. Carney, ABD merkezli X platformundaki hesabından yaptığı açıklamada, görüşmenin olumlu geçtiğini ve karşılıklı fayda sağlayacak bir ticaret anlaşmasının ana hatlarının ele alındığını bildirdi. Görüşmenin, iki ülke arasında daha önce gerçekleştirilen yapıcı temasların devamı niteliğinde olduğunu belirten Carney, hedeflenen anlaşmanın çalışanlar için istihdam yaratmasını ve ailelerin satın alma gücünü artırmasını amaçladığını ifade etti. Carney ayrıca anlaşmanın Kanada'nın dillerine, kültürüne ve egemenliğine tam anlamıyla saygı göstermesi gerektiğini vurguladı. Ekipler önümüzdeki haftalarda çalışacak Kanada Başbakanı, iki ülkenin ekiplerinin önümüzdeki haftalarda anlaşmaya yönelik sonuç elde etmek için çalışmalarını sürdüreceğini kaydetti. ABD ile Kanada arasında özellikle Trump'ın ikinci başkanlık döneminde gümrük tarifeleri ve ticaret politikaları nedeniyle gerilim yaşanmıştı. Carney, 27 Ekim'de yaptığı açıklamada, ABD'nin kırmızı çizgilerinin kabul edilmesi halinde ticaret anlaşmasına ulaşma ihtimalinin artacağını söylemişti. Trump da Michigan'da düzenlediği seçim konuşmasında Kanada ile ticaret meselesinin yakında çözüme kavuşturulacağını ifade etmişti. ABD ve Kanada ticareti neden önemli? ABD ve Kanada, birbirlerinin en büyük ticaret ortakları arasında yer alıyor. İki ülke arasındaki ticaret; otomotiv, enerji, çelik, alüminyum ve tarım gibi sektörlerde yoğunlaşıyor. Gümrük tarifelerine ilişkin anlaşmazlıklar, sınır ötesi tedarik zincirleri ve şirketlerin maliyetleri üzerinde doğrudan etkili olabiliyor.

news.title: Lindsay Clancy is back in court - where will her case go next?
news.summary: The Massachusetts mother, accused of murdering her three children, is expected back in court as she awaits a decision on whether her case will be retried.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Lindsay Clancy is back in court - where will her case go next?
news.summaryTr: The Massachusetts mother, accused of murdering her three children, is expected back in court as she awaits a decision on whether her case will be retried.
news.articleText: Lindsay Clancy is back in court - where will her case go next? - Published Lindsay Clancy, the US woman accused of murdering her three children, will return to a Massachusetts court on Monday as lawyers debate retrying the case. Her defence team and Massachusetts prosecutors are expected to discuss how to move forward, with both parties seeking different outcomes. Last week, in response to a defence request to dismiss the trial, prosecutors offered their clearest hint yet that they are seeking a new trial before a different jury. "The Commonwealth [Massachusetts] should be permitted to continue to pursue justice for Cora, Dawson and Callan Clancy," her three children, prosecutors said. Prosecutors could also reduce the charges in a potential second trial or dismiss them altogether. Clancy's first trial ended in a mistrial after a 12-person jury failed to reach a consensus. The 36-year-old has not denied killing her children in 2023, but her defence team argues she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis at the time. Prosecutors say the killings were intentional. What happened when Clancy was last in court? A jury first heard Clancy's case in August 2026, but failed to reach a unanimous agreement on whether the prosecution had proved Clancy was guilty "beyond a reasonable doubt" as required by US law. A judge declared a mistrial in early September. At a court appearance later that month, Clancy's lawyer, Kevin Reddington, argued the judge should dismiss her case. Meanwhile, prosecutors said the state had "met its burden" in proving her guilt. But the hours-long back-and-forth ultimately didn't lead to a clearer answer about what might come next for Clancy - a dismissal of charges, retrial of the same charges, or retrial of lesser charges. These discussions will resume on Monday. Judge William Sullivan seemed confident the case would be retried, saying in September he wanted to "get this thing moving". He asked both sides to prepare to discuss possible trial dates at the November hearing. Reddington said he would be unable to go to trial until at least June 2027 if the case was retried. District Attorney Timothy Cruz said at the time that prosecutors had not yet decided whether to retry Clancy. "We're doing our due diligence; we're going to continue doing that," he said. "We're going to do what we can for the children. That's what this case is about." What do Clancy's legal team want? Fundamentally, Clancy's legal team - with Reddington at the helm - is pushing for the charges to be dismissed or dropped. They've explored a variety of legal avenues. In September, he asked for her to be found not guilty under Rule 25 - a Massachusetts provision that states a defendant should be found not guilty if prosecutors do not present enough evidence at trial. That request was denied. Judge Sullivan will hear arguments on several motions on Monday, but Heather Cucolo, a New York Law School professor and mental health law expert, told the BBC that the hearing will likely focus on a narrow point: was this an instance of a routine deadlocked-jury mistrial - in which the jury genuinely could not agree - or was this an improperly terminated trial? She said Reddington may argue that a retrial could violate Clancy's Constitutional protection against double jeopardy - a legal standard that says a person cannot be tried for the same crime twice. But legal experts agree that outcome is unlikely. "The public attention that's been put on this trial and the need to have some conclusion in the near future, I think that the judge is going to say that this mistrial was appropriate, was legally accurate, and that they need to now look to set a date for a retrial," Cucolo said. What do prosecutors want? While the state's legal team has not explicitly said they will pursue a retrial, Cruz and the prosecutors who argued the case have consistently said they want justice for Clancy's children. Last week, prosecutors asked Judge Sullivan to reject the motion to dismiss charges against Clancy on the grounds of double jeopardy. They argue mistrial procedures were properly followed by the court, and thus they have a right to seek justice again on behalf of the children. "Because a mistrial was properly declared due to the manifest necessity of a deadlocked jury, the defendant's motion to dismiss should be denied," prosecutors wrote in the motion. What could happen on 2 November? Judge Sullivan could make a determination over whether the case can proceed on Monday or he could rule later in writing, criminal defence lawyer Elyse Hershon told the BBC. And how the District Attorney's office wants to proceed could be determined ahead of Monday's hearing, during it or even days after, she said. "The three charges of first-degree murder are still pending; they are still hanging over Lindsay Clancy's head unless and until the DA announces otherwise," Hershon said. Historically, Cruz, the district attorney, has made comments and announcements about the case at press conferences after court finishes. That could happen again this week, she predicted. It is also likely, Hershon said, that Judge Sullivan pushes the lawyers on both sides to get a trial date on the calendar during Monday's hearing. "It does not mean it's definitely going to be a jury trial, but [they will want to] put something in the books, hold those dates. It's a big chunk of time. It's four, five, six weeks of the court calendar; that's hard to fit in at the last minute," she said. "I would anticipate they block off the time while they go through all these motions and the DA's office figures out what it wants to do." news.titleTr: ABD seçimleri piyasaların seyrini değiştirebilir: ING'den 5 kritik başlık
news.summaryTr: ING, 3 Kasım'da yapılacak ABD ara seçimlerinin küresel ekonomi ve piyasalar üzerinde önemli etkiler yaratabileceğine dikkat çekti. Bankaya göre seçimlerin ardından Kongre'de oluşabilecek güç dengesi; Trump'ın İran politikasından gümrük tarifelerine birçok başlığı etkileyebilir.
news.articleText: ABD seçimleri piyasaların seyrini değiştirebilir: ING'den 5 kritik başlık ING, 3 Kasım'da yapılacak ABD ara seçimlerinin küresel ekonomi ve piyasalar üzerinde önemli etkiler yaratabileceğine dikkat çekti. Bankaya göre seçimlerin ardından Kongre'de oluşabilecek güç dengesi; Trump'ın İran politikasından gümrük tarifelerine birçok başlığı etkileyebilir. ABD'de 3 Kasım'da yapılacak Kongre ara seçimleri yaklaşırken, küresel piyasalar açısından olası sonuçlar da gündeme geliyor. ING, seçimlerin Ortadoğu'daki gelişmeler, yapay zeka yatırımları ve ticaret politikaları üzerinden küresel ekonomiyi etkileyebileceğini değerlendirdi. ING ekonomisti James Smith, seçimlerin ardından Washington'da bölünmüş bir yönetim ortaya çıkmasının ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'ı dış politika ve gümrük tarifeleri gibi yürütme yetkisinin daha geniş olduğu alanlara yöneltebileceğini belirtti. Demokratların Kongre'de çoğunluğu İran politikasını etkileyebilir ING'ye göre Demokratların Kongre'de çoğunluğu elde etmesi, Trump yönetiminin İran politikasında iki farklı sonuç doğurabilir. İç politikada yasama faaliyetlerinin zorlaşması, Trump'ın dış politikaya daha fazla ağırlık vermesine yol açabilir. Diğer taraftan Demokratların Kongre'deki etkisinin artması, İran savaşı ve bu savaşın finansmanına yönelik itirazları güçlendirebilir. ABD Başkan Yardımcısı JD Vance'in İran'a gönderdiği mektup diplomatik çözüm ihtimaline işaret ederken, bölgeye ilave ABD askeri kapasitesi gönderildiğine ilişkin haberler yeni saldırı olasılığını gündemde tutuyor. ING, çatışmalarda yeni bir tırmanış yaşanmaması halinde enerji fiyatlarında oluşan yüksek risk priminin bir bölümünün ortadan kalkabileceğini öngördü. Yapay zeka yatırımları seçim gündeminde ING'nin değerlendirmesinde yapay zeka yatırımlarının siyasi boyutu da öne çıktı. ABD'de yapay zeka bağlantılı yatırımların yıllık yüzde 20'nin üzerinde arttığı, diğer sektörlerdeki sermaye harcamalarının ise zayıf seyrettiği belirtildi. Özellikle veri merkezlerinin hızla yaygınlaşmasının siyasi tartışma konusu haline geldiğine dikkat çekildi. Araştırmalara göre yaklaşık 12 milyon Amerikalı bir veri merkezinin 2 kilometre yakınında yaşıyor. ING, ara seçimlerin 2028 başkanlık seçimleri öncesinde yapay zeka altyapısına yönelik yatırımların ne ölçüde siyasi tartışmaya dönüşeceğini gösterebileceğini değerlendirdi. Trump yönetiminden Avrupa'ya yeni tarife gelebilir ING, ABD'de federal bütçe açığının gayrisafi yurt içi hasılanın (GSYH) yaklaşık yüzde 6'sına ulaştığını ve Kongre'de bu açığı anlamlı ölçüde azaltmaya yönelik güçlü bir eğilim bulunmadığını belirtti. Bölünmüş yönetimin bütçe ve maliye politikalarında uzlaşmayı zorlaştırabileceğine dikkat çeken banka, Trump yönetiminin özellikle Avrupa'ya yönelik yeni gümrük tarifelerine başvurabileceği uyarısında bulundu. ABD Yüksek Mahkemesi'nin acil durum tarifelerini iptal etmesinin ardından uygulanan geçici yüzde 10'luk genel tarifelerin yerini, 301. madde kapsamında daha kalıcı bir tarife yapısının aldığı hatırlatıldı. Fed için aralık ayında faiz artışı beklentisi ING, ABD'de açıklanacak ekim ayı istihdam raporunda tarım dışı istihdamın yaklaşık 75 bin kişi artmasını, işsizlik oranının ise yüzde 4,2 seviyesinde kalmasını bekliyor. Piyasaların Fed'in 9 Aralık toplantısında faiz artırımı ihtimalini yüzde 80 olarak fiyatladığını belirten banka, bu beklentiyi makul bulduğunu bildirdi. İngiltere'de faiz artışı, Euro Bölgesi'nde yüzde 4 enflasyon beklentisi ING, İngiltere Merkez Bankası'nın gelecek perşembe günü yapılacak toplantıda 7'ye karşı 2 oyla faiz artırmasını bekliyor. Banka, şubat ayında ikinci bir faiz artışının da gündeme gelebileceğini öngörüyor. Euro Bölgesi'nde ise yükselen enerji maliyetleri nedeniyle enflasyonun gelecek hafta yüzde 4'e ulaşabileceği tahmin ediliyor. Doğalgaz fiyatlarındaki yükselişin sürmesi halinde enflasyon üzerindeki yukarı yönlü risklerin devam edeceği belirtiliyor. ING'ye göre Avrupa Merkez Bankası, önümüzdeki dönemde özellikle enerji dışındaki fiyat gelişmelerini, çekirdek enflasyonu ve gıda fiyatlarını yakından izleyecek. ABD ara seçimleri neden piyasalar için önemli? ABD ara seçimleri, başkanın görev süresinin ikinci yılında Kongre'nin Temsilciler Meclisi ve Senato kanadındaki sandalye dağılımını yeniden belirliyor. Kongre'de çoğunluğun el değiştirmesi; bütçe, vergi düzenlemeleri, ticaret politikaları ve dış politika kararlarının uygulanmasını etkileyebiliyor. Bu nedenle seçim sonuçları yalnızca ABD piyasaları değil, dolar, tahvil faizleri, enerji fiyatları ve küresel ticaret açısından da yakından takip ediliyor.

news.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
news.summary: Five officers from the Hamas-run police have been killed in Khan Younis and three people, including a child, killed in Gaza City, officials say.

news.titleTr: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
news.summaryTr: Five officers from the Hamas-run police have been killed in Khan Younis and three people, including a child, killed in Gaza City, officials say.
news.articleText: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say - Published Israeli strikes in Gaza have killed at least eight people, including a child, according to hospitals, despite a year-old ceasefire. In Gaza City to the north, hospital officials said a missile attack hit a group of civilians next to Cairo School in the Al-Rimal neighbourhood, killing three people, including a four-year-old boy. In the southern city of Khan Younis, the Hamas-run ministry of interior said a drone attack targeted a group of police officers in the Al-Mawasi area, killing five, as they were carrying out their routine duties. The Israeli military said it had carried out two attacks on what it described as military operatives but has not yet provided evidence or further information. Outside Gaza City's Shifa Hospital, video showed a crowd of men gathered to pray next to two body bags and the tiny body of the child, which was wrapped in a white towel. "My son and his child were martyred. They were sitting in their tent, bothering no one, and nothing else was happening in the area when suddenly, a missile struck them, and they were martyred," Ali Oweis told AFP news agency. "There is no ceasefire; the war is ongoing, don't you see?" At Nasser hospital in Khan Younis, women despaired as body bags lay on the floor, video showed. The interior ministry named the five police officers killed, who were between the ages of 23 and 53, and called the attack a "horrific massacre". A ceasefire came into force in Gaza in October last year, but Israeli air strikes have continued almost every day. Since then, 1,580 people have been killed, according to Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. Israel says it is targeting Hamas, but often civilians are also killed. Meanwhile, a peace plan for Gaza, brokered by the Trump administration, has stalled. The ceasefire saw thousands of Palestinians held by Israel released in return for all of the 48 remaining hostages held in Gaza, and an agreement to end the war. The conflict was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage. Since the war began, 74,594 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the territory's health ministry. Additional reporting by Jacob Phillips Related topics - Published19 October

A ceasefire came into force in Gaza in October last year, but Israeli air strikes have continued almost every day. Since then, 1,580 people have been killed, according to Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. Israel says it is targeting Hamas, but often civilians are also killed. Meanwhile, a peace plan for Gaza, brokered by the Trump administration, has stalled. The ceasefire saw thousands of Palestinians held by Israel released in return for all of the 48 remaining hostages held in Gaza, and an agreement to end the war. The conflict was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage. Since the war began, 74,594 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the territory's health ministry. Additional reporting by Jacob Phillips Related topics - Published19 October

news.summary: Marta Shahbazi was an "inspiring, talented and passionate scientist", says the laboratory where she worked.

news.titleTr: University of Cambridge scientist among those who died in Spanish train crash
news.summaryTr: Marta Shahbazi was an "inspiring, talented and passionate scientist", says the laboratory where she worked.
news.articleText: Cambridge scientist dies in Spanish train crash - Published An award-winning University of Cambridge researcher died in the Spanish train disaster while on her way to collect a prize for scientific excellence. Dr Marta Shahbazi was travelling to an awards ceremony on Wednesday when the train she was on crashed into another near Urda, south of Madrid, killing 69 people. The mother of two was an affiliate associate professor leading a group of researchers at MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB) in Cambridge and had earned several awards for work on human embryos and cell biology. In a statement, the LMB paid tribute to the "inspiring, talented and passionate scientist" and described her death as a "profound shock and a huge loss". The expert in cell biology ran the Shahbazi Laboratory at the LMB, based on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus. She had been announced as the winner of a Spanish Society for Developmental Biology award for her contributions to the study of early human development and was due to collect the award at a conference in El Rompido in Andalusia. The LMB said: "As a wife and mother of two young children, Marta wrote eloquently about balancing her family and career, serving as a much-admired role model for a 'mother scientist', a term she used to describe herself. "Marta was an inspiring, talented and passionate scientist whose research shed light on the earliest steps in the development of human embryos and how errors occur that lead to failed pregnancies," the LMB said. The institute said her death was "a profound shock and a huge loss for LMB". Her work had been recognised with "many awards and prizes", the laboratory added. Shahbazi is listed on the University of Cambridge website as a principal investigator at its Stem Cell Institute (CSCI). Institute director Prof Bertie Gottgens said its community was "shocked and deeply saddened" by her death. "Marta led her primary research group at the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB) alongside her roles as an affiliate principal investigator and affiliate assistant professor at the CSCI," he said. "Across both institutes, she was highly respected for her pioneering research on early human development and valued for her collaborative spirit. "Her creativity, passion, and generosity will be greatly missed." The news of her death was first confirmed in a social media post, external by the CiMUS, based in Santiago de Compostela where Shahbazi's aunt works. Shahbazi undertook her PhD at the Spanish National Cancer Research Centre, before joining the University of Cambridge as a post-doctoral fellow and then the LMB in 2020. The crash in Spain happened when a state-operated Renfe high-speed train smashed into the back of a stationary train operated by the Iryo company. It is one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's modern history, and Spain's worst crash since 2013. Three days of national mourning were declared in the country. More than 540 people were on board both trains. Get in touch Your Voice Follow Cambridgeshire news on BBC Sounds, Facebook, external, Instagram, external and X, external.

news.title: Thousands of jobs at Virgin Media O2 to be cut
news.summary: The broadband provider has not finalised the number of roles to be axed but it will likely be a sizeable chunk of its workforce, the BBC understands.
